quality_snapshot.text:
The rain drummed steadily against the windowpane, a relentless symphony that blurred the world outside into a watercolor of grays and blues. Claire pressed her forehead against the cool glass, the chill seeping into her skin, grounding her in this dim-lit room where shadows danced in the corners, stretching and contracting with each flicker of the aging bulb overhead. She inhaled deeply, the musty scent of old books and damp paper filling her lungs, a reminder of the library where she had spent countless hours escaping into other lives.

“Another storm,” she muttered, more to the universe than to herself. The words hung in the air, heavy with resignation. She turned away from the window, her heart a heavy drum in her chest. The room felt too vast, too empty—a hollow echo of what it once was. A flicker of movement caught her eye; the cat, a fluffy tabby named Horace, slinked across the floor, pausing to nuzzle against her ankle before continuing his patrol of the room.

“Even you can’t chase away the gloom, can you?” she said softly, bending down to scratch behind his ears. He responded with a purr, the sound vibrating through her fingertips, a brief solace against the encroaching thoughts that clung to her mind like mist.

Outside, a flash of lightning illuminated the sky, momentarily casting the room in stark relief. Claire’s heart raced at the sight, each heartbeat echoing the tumult of the storm. She could almost feel the electricity crackling in the air, a reminder of the chaos that lay beyond the safe confines of her home. The world outside was fierce, alive with a wildness she felt both drawn to and terrified of, an uninvited guest in her own life.

“Get a grip, Claire,” she whispered, shaking her head as if to dislodge the weight of her swirling thoughts.
